\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جلد} \ur{بازی} (jald-bāzī)}{جلد بازی (jald-bāzī)}]{\ur{جلد} \ur{بازی} (jald-bāzī) — haste; rushing}

\label{lesson:UR-C370-jald-bazi}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to pester, then the Urdu for to throw away.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جلد} \ur{بازی}}
\textbf{\ur{جلد} \ur{بازی}} — \emph{jald-bāzī} — \textquotedblleft{}haste; rushing\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{جلد} \ur{بازی} \ur{کی} \ur{تو} \ur{حادثہ} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne jald-bāzī kī to hādsā ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you rush, there will be an accident.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جلد} \ur{بازی}} (\emph{jald-bāzī}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{jaldbāzī}, \textquotedblleft{}haste\textquotedblright{}: \emph{jald}, \textquotedblleft{}quick\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{bāzī}, \textquotedblleft{}play\textquotedblright{}. Playing at speed.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jald-bāzī}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jald-bāzī}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne jald-bāzī kī to hādsā ho gā.} — If you rush, there will be an accident.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to pester, then the Urdu for to throw away, then say \emph{jald-bāzī} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جلد} \ur{بازی} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Haste; rushing\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دھیان} (dhyān)}{دھیان (dhyān)}]{\ur{دھیان} (dhyān) — attention; care}

\label{lesson:UR-C370-dhyan}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to throw away, then the Urdu for haste.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دھیان}}
\textbf{\ur{دھیان}} — \emph{dhyān} — \textquotedblleft{}attention; care\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{دھیان} \ur{سے} \ur{چلیے،} \ur{ورنہ} \ur{آپ} \ur{گر} \ur{جائیں} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dhyān se chaliye, varnā āp gir jāeṅ ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Walk carefully, or you will fall.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دھیان}} (\emph{dhyān}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{dhyāna}, \textquotedblleft{}meditation, thought\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6889); in Urdu, the mind kept on what you are doing.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhyān}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dhyān se chaliye, varnā āp gir jāeṅ ge.} — Walk carefully, or you will fall.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to throw away, then the Urdu for haste, then say \emph{dhyān} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{صبر} (sabr)}{صبر (sabr)}]{\ur{صبر} (sabr) — patience}

\label{lesson:UR-C370-sabr}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for haste, then the Urdu for attention.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{صبر}}
\textbf{\ur{صبر}} — \emph{sabr} — \textquotedblleft{}patience\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{صبر} \ur{کریں} \ur{گے} \ur{تو} \ur{سب} \ur{ٹھیک} \ur{ہو} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp sabr kareṅ ge to sab ṭhīk ho gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}

\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{صبر}} (\emph{sabr}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ṣabr}, \textquotedblleft{}patience, endurance\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{پھوڑنا} (phoṛnā)}{پھوڑنا (phoṛnā)}]{\ur{پھوڑنا} (phoṛnā) — to smash; to break (something brittle)}

\label{lesson:UR-C370-phorna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for attention, then the Urdu for patience.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{پھوڑنا}}
\textbf{\ur{پھوڑنا}} — \emph{phoṛnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to smash; to break (something brittle)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{تم} \ur{نے} \ur{جلدی} \ur{کی} \ur{تو} \ur{برتن} \ur{پھوڑ} \ur{دو} \ur{گے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar tum ne jaldī kī to bartan phoṛ do ge.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you hurry, you will smash the dishes.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{برتن} \ur{پھوڑا}, \emph{us ne bartan phoṛā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{پھوڑنا}} (\emph{phoṛnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{phoṛnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to break\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{sphōṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}bursts\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13857).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{phoṛnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar tum ne jaldī kī to bartan phoṛ do ge.} — If you hurry, you will smash the dishes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for attention, then the Urdu for patience, then say \emph{phoṛnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{مسلنا} (masalnā)}{مسلنا (masalnā)}]{\ur{مسلنا} (masalnā) — to crush; to squash}

\label{lesson:UR-C370-masalna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for patience, then the Urdu for to smash.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{مسلنا}}
\textbf{\ur{مسلنا}} — \emph{masalnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crush; to squash\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اگر} \ur{آپ} \ur{نے} \ur{کیڑا} \ur{مسلا} \ur{تو} \ur{وہ} \ur{مر} \ur{جائے} \ur{گا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{agar āp ne kīṛā maslā to voh mar jāe gā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
If you squash the insect, it will die.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پھول} \ur{مسلا}, \emph{us ne phūl maslā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{مسلنا}} (\emph{masalnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{masalnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to rub to pieces\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{maṣati} (CDIAL 9919).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for saying what happens if.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masalnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{masalnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{agar āp ne kīṛā maslā to voh mar jāe gā.} — If you squash the insect, it will die.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for patience, then the Urdu for to smash, then say \emph{masalnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from Hopes and Fears to Haste and Care}

\label{lesson:UR-R370-review-363-370}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for an apprehension and a hint.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item an apprehension, a hint, a symptom, a nagging fear, confidence
  \item evident, compulsory, really, prominent, to emerge
  \item a state, a situation, a hardship, a change, to land in trouble
  \item only, except, permission, on no account, to forbid
  \item mere, a regulation, a breach, a clause, to come into force
  \item a hassle, an obstacle, a solution, to get stuck, to deal with
  \item if only, a longing, a wistful regret, to pester, to throw away
  \item haste, attention, patience, to smash, to squash
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
An apprehension? (\textbf{\ur{اندیشہ}}, \emph{andeshā}.) A hint? (\textbf{\ur{اشارہ}}, \emph{ishārā}.) A symptom? (\textbf{\ur{علامت}}, \emph{alāmat}.) A nagging fear? (\textbf{\ur{خدشہ}}, \emph{khadshā}.) Confidence? (\textbf{\ur{اعتماد}}, \emph{etimād}.) Evident? (\textbf{\ur{ظاہر}}, \emph{zāhir}.) Compulsory? (\textbf{\ur{لازمی}}, \emph{lāzmī}.) Really? (\textbf{\ur{واقعی}}, \emph{vāqaī}.) Prominent? (\textbf{\ur{نمایاں}}, \emph{numāyāṅ}.) To emerge? (\textbf{\ur{ابھرنا}}, \emph{ubharnā}.) A state? (\textbf{\ur{حالت}}, \emph{hālat}.) A situation? (\textbf{\ur{صورت} \ur{حال}}, \emph{sūrat-e-hāl}.) A hardship? (\textbf{\ur{مصیبت}}, \emph{musībat}.) A change? (\textbf{\ur{تبدیلی}}, \emph{tabdīlī}.) To land in trouble? (\textbf{\ur{پھنسانا}}, \emph{phansānā}.) Only? (\textbf{\ur{صرف}}, \emph{sirf}.) Except? (\textbf{\ur{سوائے}}, \emph{sivāe}.) Permission? (\textbf{\ur{اجازت}}, \emph{ijāzat}.) On no account? (\textbf{\ur{ہرگز}}, \emph{hargiz}.) To forbid? (\textbf{\ur{منع} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{manā karnā}.) Mere? (\textbf{\ur{محض}}, \emph{mahz}.) A regulation? (\textbf{\ur{قاعدہ}}, \emph{qāidā}.) A breach? (\textbf{\ur{خلاف} \ur{ورزی}}, \emph{khilāf-varzī}.) A clause? (\textbf{\ur{شق}}, \emph{shiq}.) To come into force? (\textbf{\ur{نافذ} \ur{ہونا}}, \emph{nāfiz honā}.) A hassle? (\textbf{\ur{دقت}}, \emph{diqqat}.) An obstacle? (\textbf{\ur{رکاوٹ}}, \emph{rukāvaṭ}.) A solution? (\textbf{\ur{حل}}, \emph{hal}.) To get stuck? (\textbf{\ur{اٹکنا}}, \emph{aṭaknā}.) To deal with? (\textbf{\ur{نبٹانا}}, \emph{nibṭānā}.) If only? (\textbf{\ur{کاش}}, \emph{kāsh}.) A longing? (\textbf{\ur{ارمان}}, \emph{armān}.) A wistful regret? (\textbf{\ur{حسرت}}, \emph{hasrat}.) To pester? (\textbf{\ur{ستانا}}, \emph{satānā}.) To throw away? (\textbf{\ur{گنوانا}}, \emph{ganvānā}.) Haste? (\textbf{\ur{جلد} \ur{بازی}}, \emph{jald-bāzī}.) Attention? (\textbf{\ur{دھیان}}, \emph{dhyān}.) Patience? (\textbf{\ur{صبر}}, \emph{sabr}.) To smash? (\textbf{\ur{پھوڑنا}}, \emph{phoṛnā}.) To squash? (\textbf{\ur{مسلنا}}, \emph{masalnā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
